name: Land Dayak (Retired)
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Retired Glottolog bookkeeping entry: Land Dayak is a family name (Bidayuhic), not a language; no language to describe

new_statements.quote: In Bidayuh the ultima (last syllable) is the nucleus of the word. It receives the peak of word stress—at least in citation forms (words that are pronounced individually). The ultima can have a somewhat more complex structure and a greater variety of phonological content than other syllables. [...] In some words of the shape (C)V.V(C), in western dialects (Singai, Jagoi) and also in Rara, the same vowel occurs in both the ultima (last syllable) and the penult (second-to-last syllable). In such words initiation of stress (accent) on the ultima vowel is usually perceptible: (C)V1.ˈV1(C). [fn. 79, p. 95:] Because word stress falls on the final syllable in Bidayuh citation forms, and perhaps in context, a clitic receives the stress placement in the word to which it is attached.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Across the Bidayuh (Sarawak Land Dayak) dialects, word stress falls on the final syllable (ultima) of the word, at least in citation forms; the ultima is the phonologically richest syllable (all six vowels, contrastive length in eastern/central dialects), pretonic syllables have reduced vowel inventories.
new_statements.exceptions: Post-clitics (e.g. 3sg clitic) attach like suffixes and take the word stress (fn. 79). Hedge 'at least in citation forms.. and perhaps in context'. No lexical exceptions mentioned.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly citation forms (words pronounced individually); author leaves connected-speech placement open ('perhaps in context'). Statement is family/dialect-cluster-wide (Biatah, Bukar-Sadung, Bau-Jagoi/Singai, Tringgus etc., plus Rara Bakati'), not tied to one ISO language.
new_statements.identity_note: land1262 is not a language: it is Glottolog's Bookkeeping placeholder for ISO 639-3 [dyk] 'Dayak, Land', retired 2008-01-14 (CR 2007-254) because 'Land Dayak' is the family name now called Bidayuhic/Land Dayak, whose members already have codes. The quoted statement (Rensch et al. 2012) is a family-wide description of the Sarawak Bidayuh dialect cluster and belongs under the constituent languages, which have their own check dirs/targets: Biatah biat1246 (same book + Rensch 2006/2008 'Stress falls on the ultima'), Bukar-Sadong buka1257, Bau-Jagoi baub1235, Tringgus-Sembaan trin1271; further Land Dayak branches are Bakati' (Rara, Sara) and Southern Land Dayak (Kembayan, Ribun, Semandang) in Kalimantan. by our rule that each source is filed under the language's current Glottolog code (a retired code does not make a separate language) no catalog row should be created for land1262.
